messages.body_plain:
Dear Elena,
Try using the statnet.org repository.  It's not a CRAN mirror, but (unlike CRAN) it has the most current version of the statnet package.  

To do this, try 
install.packages("statnet", repos="http://www.csde.washington.edu/statnet")

This might not work, as it appears that the problem you're having is with rgl rather than any of the statnet packages.  However, if I remember correctly, there is no strict dependence on rgl in the new statnet so you might be okay.

Best wishes,
Dave

install.packages("statnet", rep

messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] add a legend to a graph
messages.body_plain:
Hi Bjorn,

I've had a similar problem in the past.  If you save the output of the
plotting command, something like:

 p1 = plot(newnet1, etc....)
>

you'll see that the coordinates of all the points are saved, and that these
are not the same from one call to plot to the next.

So, you can pull out the coordinates from "p1" (by taking say the min or
max of the x or y values).  More often though, I will just use:

legend("bottomright", legend = etc...),

or "topleft" or "topright" or "bottomleft", as this will ensure the legend
is in the proper space.

HTH,

ayn
